facts.text: It started about a month after the abnormal sensations had gone away.

facts.item: abnormal sensations on the right side of the body
facts.text: I had abnormal sensations on the right side of my body.
They began in my right lower leg as pins and needles.
Along with the pins and needles, things that should only hurt a little hurt much more (hyperalgesia).
They spread up my leg; then the leg symptoms went away, and similar sensations appeared in my right arm, tongue and face.
Altogether the abnormal sensations went on for about three months, and then they went away.

facts.item: abnormal sensations on the left side
facts.text: My left side was never affected.
Nothing I can think of set them off.
I haven't had any whole-body symptoms.
I don't have any significant medical problems.
I don't have any risk factors for blood vessel disease.

gold.reasoning: 1. MOG‐antibody–associated disease was excluded because it “do not present with Dawson finger findings in MRI and lack specific oligoclonal G bands (Oligo-G) in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis.” 2. Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders were considered unlikely since “Dawson’s fingers and jagged-border periventricular hyperintensities are a rare entity in NMO spectrum disorders but a common feature of MS.”

source_issues: The dysesthesia is said to have resolved (s004), but the examination finds right-sided facial sensory loss (s008).
s001 ('presented with a 3-month history') and s004 (referral after the later vertigo) describe the presentation at two points; the timeline is reconstructed in the facts.
notes: Index visit: the referral neurologic evaluation after the onset of vertigo (s004–s011); the right-sided sensory episodes (s001–s003) are history that has resolved, and the MRI two months after vertigo onset (s012) is given a time.
Slight anxiety is an observer sign kept in the mental status finding; the facial sensory loss is an examination finding only because the patient's dysesthesia had resolved.
f010 is a blanket denial of systemic symptoms; f013 a blanket denial of vascular risk factors, which does not answer specific questions such as smoking or blood pressure.
